status.en: 222 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Plateau State.
status.nb: 222 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Plateau State.

summary.en: Gunmen killed an NSCDC officer and abducted a businessman in Plateau despite a curfew, and gunmen attacked an Ebonyi assembly candidate convoy, killing one and injuring three. In Benue, suspected herders killed three civilians and Senate leaders are demanding a security overhaul and troop deployment after 113 people were killed, while electricity workers withdrew services in Makurdi following an alleged attack. Bandits continue to hold a widow, her son and a newborn captive three weeks after a kidnapping in Kaduna, and a NDC supporter was killed in Enugu. Floods killed 245 people and displaced over 200,000, according to NEMA, and the conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenmenn drepte en NSCDC-offiser og bortførte en forretningsmann i Plateau til tross for portforbud, og våpenmenn angrep en kandidatkonvoi for Ebonyi-forsamlingen, drepte én og såret tre. I Benue drepte mistenkte hyrdegrupper tre sivile, og senatets ledere krever en sikkerhetsreform og utplassering av tropper etter at 113 personer ble drept, mens strømarbeidere avbrøt tjenestene i Makurdi etter et påstått angrep. Banditter holder fortsatt en enke, hennes sønn og et nyfødt som fange tre uker etter en kidnapping i Kaduna, og en NDC-tilhenger ble drept i Enugu. Flommer drepte 245 personer og fordrev over 200 000, ifølge NEMA, og konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
